questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: What does it mean to lease a car?

choices.text: Buying the car outright with one cash payment
Paying to use it for a set term, then returning it
Borrowing to buy the car and keeping it after payoff
Renting a car for one weekend trip

questions.correct_answer: Paying to use it for a set term, then returning it
questions.intro: A lease is a long-term rental, often 2 to 4 years. You pay for the car's expected loss in value plus a finance charge, then return it or buy it at a set price.
questions.feedback: A lease pays for use over a term; ownership stays with the leasing company.
sources: FTC (Financing or leasing a car): A lease lets a consumer use a vehicle for a set term; leases have mileage limits, wear-and-tear charges, and early termination costs. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/financing-or-leasing-car)

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: A lease allows 10,000 miles a year for 3 years and charges $0.25 for each extra mile. Maya drives 36,000 miles. What is the charge?
questions.intro: Leases have mileage limits. Extra miles are charged at a set rate when the car is returned.

misconceptions.C: Gives the extra miles, not dollars

sources: FTC (Financing or leasing a car): A lease lets a consumer use a vehicle for a set term; leases have mileage limits, wear-and-tear charges, and early termination costs. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/financing-or-leasing-car)

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: A car has a capitalized cost of $30,000 and a residual value of $18,000 after 36 months. What is the monthly depreciation part of the payment?
questions.intro: Capitalized cost is the lease's agreed price. Residual value is the predicted value at the end. The payment covers the depreciation (cap cost − residual) spread over the months, plus a finance charge and tax.
sources: FTC (Financing or leasing a car): A lease lets a consumer use a vehicle for a set term; leases have mileage limits, wear-and-tear charges, and early termination costs. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/financing-or-leasing-car)

misconceptions.B: Leaves out the amount due at signing

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Who is usually a better fit for leasing?

choices.text: A driver who goes 25,000 miles a year and keeps cars a decade
A buyer who wants to customize the car and own it outright
A person who wants never to have a monthly car payment
A low-mileage driver who wants a new car often

questions.correct_answer: A low-mileage driver who wants a new car often
questions.intro: Leasing tends to fit drivers who stay under mileage limits, keep the car in good shape, and like changing cars every few years. Buying fits drivers who keep cars a long time.
questions.feedback: Leasing fits low mileage and frequent upgrades.
sources: FTC (Financing or leasing a car): A lease lets a consumer use a vehicle for a set term; leases have mileage limits, wear-and-tear charges, and early termination costs. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/financing-or-leasing-car)

sections.relationship: A lease is paying to use; a loan is paying to own. The difference explains every lease term.

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: At the end of a lease, what can the driver usually do?

choices.text: Return the car or buy it at the set price
Keep the car free of charge forever
Sell the car and keep the money
Stop paying and drive it until it finally breaks

questions.correct_answer: Return the car or buy it at the set price
questions.intro: The lease contract states a purchase option price, often equal to the residual value.
questions.feedback: Return the car or buy it at the contract price.

misconceptions.C: The driver does not own it

sources: FTC (Financing or leasing a car): A lease lets a consumer use a vehicle for a set term; leases have mileage limits, wear-and-tear charges, and early termination costs. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/financing-or-leasing-car)

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: In a lease, what is the residual value?

choices.text: The amount paid up front at signing
The predicted value at the end
The monthly finance charge
The car's price when new

questions.correct_answer: The predicted value at the end
questions.feedback: Residual value is the expected value when the lease ends.
sources: FTC (Financing or leasing a car): A lease lets a consumer use a vehicle for a set term; leases have mileage limits, wear-and-tear charges, and early termination costs. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/financing-or-leasing-car)

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: What are "excess wear and tear" charges?

choices.text: Monthly fees for routine oil changes
Taxes on the car's registration
Fees for damage beyond normal use
Charges for driving under the mileage limit

questions.correct_answer: Fees for damage beyond normal use
questions.intro: Lessees return the car in the condition the lease requires. Dents, stains, and worn tires beyond the standard can be charged.
questions.feedback: Damage beyond normal wear is charged at return.
sources: FTC (Financing or leasing a car): A lease lets a consumer use a vehicle for a set term; leases have mileage limits, wear-and-tear charges, and early termination costs. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/financing-or-leasing-car)

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: After paying off a car loan, the owner has the car. After a lease ends, what does the driver own?

choices.text: Half of the car's value
The car, with no further cost
Nothing, unless they buy the car
A credit toward any future purchase

questions.correct_answer: Nothing, unless they buy the car
questions.intro: Equity is the value you own. Loan payments build equity; lease payments do not.
questions.feedback: A lease builds no ownership; a paid-off loan does.
sources: FTC (Financing or leasing a car): A lease lets a consumer use a vehicle for a set term; leases have mileage limits, wear-and-tear charges, and early termination costs. (https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/financing-or-leasing-car)

questions.prompt: A lease has a money factor of 0.0025. Multiply by 2,400 to compare with an APR. What APR does it equal?
questions.intro: Leases state the finance charge as a money factor, a small decimal. Money factor × 2,400 is roughly the equivalent APR.

misconceptions.A: Reads the money factor as a percent

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Why do some experts advise against a large down payment on a lease?

choices.text: Down payments on leases earn very high interest
It may be lost if the car is totaled
Leasing companies are not allowed to accept them
It always raises the monthly payment

questions.correct_answer: It may be lost if the car is totaled
questions.intro: If a leased car is totaled early, insurance and GAP coverage pay the leasing company; money paid up front is usually not returned.
questions.feedback: Cash paid up front on a lease can be lost if the car is totaled.

misconceptions.A: Confuses a down payment with savings

questions.domain: Buying, Financing, and Owning a Vehicle
questions.prompt: Maya wants to end her lease after 18 of 36 months. What should she expect?

choices.text: Early termination charges
A refund of every payment made so far
No cost, since leases can end at any time
Ownership of half the car

questions.intro: Ending a lease early often triggers large fees, sometimes most of the remaining payments.
questions.feedback: Early termination usually costs a lot; read that section before signing.
